injectables.description:
Injects a component's global stylesheet once per application. A style host is an empty component (template: '', ViewEncapsulation.None) whose only payload is its styleUrl; Angular adds a component's CSS to the document when the component is created, so creating the host detached — never attached to the DOM — is enough. Directives, which have no template of their own, bring their CSS this way; components share a stylesheet the same way.

Example :
constructor() {
  inject(MudStyleLoader).load(_MudBadgeStyles);
}

directives.description:
Example :
<li mudBreadcrumbItem><a routerLink="/servicii">Servicii</a></li>
<li mudBreadcrumbItem active><span>Cerere nouă</span></li>

Sits on the <li>, so the trail is a real <nav><ol><li> list; the consumer's own anchor stays inside it and keeps routerLink. ARIA state and the tooltip are redirected onto that anchor — see target().

The truncation tooltip is driven by text(), which falls back to element.textContent — a non-reactive DOM read, so it only re-evaluates when the label input changes, not when projected content changes on its own.

Off by default, because a banner already present at page load would interrupt the screen reader mid-read, and an assertive one would cut off whatever was being announced.

  consumer-owned via `selectedChange`.
- `type="input"`: a discrete user-entered value. The body is static (no
  dead tab stop); with `removable`, a trailing close button emits `removed`.

```html
<mud-chip selectionMode="multi" [(selected)]="active" [count]="12">Acte</mud-chip>
<mud-chip type="input" removable (removed)="drop(tag)">{{ tag }}</mud-chip>
```

One choice inside an {@link MudSegmentedControl}. Applied to a native button so the DOM matches the design-system CSS contract (.segmented-control > .segment-item).

Keep labels short; an unavoidable long label truncates to one line with an ellipsis. Truncation is visual-only (the full text stays in the accessible name). components.description:
Switch — an instant on/off toggle. A native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> (the official a11y pattern) drives a styled track + thumb; the label toggles on click.

Works with BOTH forms systems:

  • Signal forms via the FormCheckboxControl contract (<mud-switch [formField]="form.notifications" /> binds checked).
  • Reactive/template-driven forms via ControlValueAccessor (boolean value).
  • Standalone via the two-way [(checked)] model.

Deliberately minimal like the official switch: one size, no invalid / readonly / supporting-text states. Associate an external message via aria-describedby when needed.

Example :
<mud-switch [formControl]="notifications">
  <mud-label>Notificări prin e-mail</mud-label>
</mud-switch>

variables.defaultValue:
(o: SnippetOptions): string => {
  const badge = o.template.includes('<mud-badge');
  const imports = ['MudTreeItem', 'MudIconComponent', 'RouterLink', ...(badge ? ['MudBadge'] : []), ...(o.tag ? ['MudTag'] : [])];

  return [
    "import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component } from '@angular/core';",
    "import { RouterLink } from '@angular/router';",
    ...(badge ? ["import { MudBadge } from 'ngx-mud-ui/badge';"] : []),
    "import { MudIconComponent } from 'ngx-mud-ui/icons';",
    ...(o.tag ? ["import { MudTag } from 'ngx-mud-ui/tag';"] : []),
    "import { MudTreeItem } from 'ngx-mud-ui/tree-item';",
    '',
    '@Component({',
    `  selector: '${o.selector}',`,
    `  imports: [${imports.join(', ')}],`,
    '  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,',
    `  template: ${BT}`,
    indent(o.template, 4),
    `  ${BT},`,
    '})',
    `export class ${o.className} {}`,
  ].join('\n');
}

so `[formField]` binds the value and the disabled state. It has no error
region or `errors` input of its own — a segmented control is a view
switcher, not a field — so the message reads the field's own `errors()`
and is rendered beside it.

functions.name: formatMasked
functions.rawdescription:
Strips everything that isn't a digit, then walks the segment spec inserting
the separator between segments. Typing `1504` yields `15/04`, so the
separator is never something the user has to press.

The separator is LAZY — emitted only when a following digit exists — exactly
as `phone-input`'s `phone-mask` does it. Appending it the instant a segment
filled (`15` → `15/`) made the field un-deletable: Backspace removes the
`/`, the re-mask puts it straight back, and the user can never delete the
month, never the day, and never clear the field with Backspace at all.

functions.name: withSwappedVirtualConsole
functions.description:
jsdom has no real navigation: clicking a real <a href> whose default was not prevented makes jsdom attempt to navigate, which logs "Not implemented: navigation to another Document" straight to process.stderr — jsdom's VirtualConsole forwards jsdomError there directly, bypassing console spies entirely (verified by instrumenting process.stderr.write directly; a vi.spyOn(console, 'error') sees nothing even though the warning still prints).

For a test that deliberately leaves a click's default un-prevented (to prove open-in-new-tab still works), this swaps the VirtualConsole's jsdomError listener for a spy for the duration of run, so the resulting navigation attempt is captured instead of printed to the test output — and is itself the strongest evidence the click's default was genuinely left alone, since a buggy guard could satisfy defaultPrevented === false via an unrelated early return without ever reaching real navigation. The original listeners are always restored, even if run throws.

Example :
const navigationAttempted = await withSwappedVirtualConsole(async () => {
  el.dispatchEvent(event);
  await fixture.whenStable();
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
});

expect(navigationAttempted).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
  expect.objectContaining({ message: expect.stringContaining('Not implemented') }),
);

    '',

    `  selector: '${o.selector}',`,
    `  imports: [${imports.join(', ')}],`,
    '  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,',
    `  template: ${BT}`,
    indent(o.template, 4),
    `  ${BT},`,

    `export class ${o.className} {}`,

}

projects/ngx-mud-ui/src/stories/componen.rawdescription:
The library deliberately does NOT auto-add tooltips to truncated labels:
truncation is visual-only (screen readers get the full text), and
detecting it would couple this entry point to the CDK overlay. When a
long label is unavoidable, compose `mudTooltip` from
`ngx-mud-ui/tooltip` on the same button — the segment IS the button, so
directives stack directly. Apply it unconditionally or gate it on your
own truncation check.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/src/stories/componen.defaultValue:
`
@Component({
  imports: [MudStepper, MudStep, ReactiveFormsModule],
  template: \`
    <mud-stepper #stepper [linear]="true">
      <mud-step
        label="Identity"
        supportingText="Who you are"
        errorMessage="Complete your identity"
        [stepControl]="identity"
      >
        <form [formGroup]="identity">
          <input formControlName="name" />
        </form>
      </mud-step>
      <mud-step label="Address" supportingText="Where you live" [stepControl]="address">
        <form [formGroup]="address">
          <input formControlName="street" />
        </form>
      </mud-step>
      <mud-step label="Review">All done — review your data.</mud-step>
    </mud-stepper>

    <button type="button" (click)="stepper.previous()">Back</button>
    <button type="button" (click)="stepper.next()">Next</button>
  \`,
})
export class ApplicationWizard {
  // \`linear\` blocks moving forward until the current step's control is valid,
  // so it only does anything when steps carry a stepControl.
  readonly identity = new FormGroup({ name: new FormControl('', Validators.required) });
  readonly address = new FormGroup({ street: new FormControl('', Validators.required) });
}
`

Task 14 needed an extra clause here — when the nth digit was the LAST one
typed and a just-auto-inserted separator followed it, the caret had to land
after that separator, or it would visibly stall one position short of where
forward typing continues. `formatMasked`'s separator is now lazy, so a

the end of the string and there is no separator left to step over. The
clause was removed with the bug that made it necessary.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.name: formatMasked
projects/ngx-mud-ui/date-picker/src/lib/.rawdescription:
Strips everything that isn't a digit, then walks the segment spec inserting
the separator between segments. Typing `1504` yields `15/04`, so the
separator is never something the user has to press.

The separator is LAZY — emitted only when a following digit exists — exactly
as `phone-input`'s `phone-mask` does it. Appending it the instant a segment
filled (`15` → `15/`) made the field un-deletable: Backspace removes the
`/`, the re-mask puts it straight back, and the user can never delete the
month, never the day, and never clear the field with Backspace at all.

projects/ngx-mud-ui/breadcrumb/src/lib/v.name: withSwappedVirtualConsole
projects/ngx-mud-ui/breadcrumb/src/lib/v.description:
jsdom has no real navigation: clicking a real <a href> whose default was not prevented makes jsdom attempt to navigate, which logs "Not implemented: navigation to another Document" straight to process.stderr — jsdom's VirtualConsole forwards jsdomError there directly, bypassing console spies entirely (verified by instrumenting process.stderr.write directly; a vi.spyOn(console, 'error') sees nothing even though the warning still prints).

For a test that deliberately leaves a click's default un-prevented (to prove open-in-new-tab still works), this swaps the VirtualConsole's jsdomError listener for a spy for the duration of run, so the resulting navigation attempt is captured instead of printed to the test output — and is itself the strongest evidence the click's default was genuinely left alone, since a buggy guard could satisfy defaultPrevented === false via an unrelated early return without ever reaching real navigation. The original listeners are always restored, even if run throws.

Example :
const navigationAttempted = await withSwappedVirtualConsole(async () => {
  el.dispatchEvent(event);
  await fixture.whenStable();
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
});

expect(navigationAttempted).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
  expect.objectContaining({ message: expect.stringContaining('Not implemented') }),
